notes: All advertised tools are registered unconditionally in `dist/index.js`; there is no source-shown feature flag or disabled-by-default toolset that removes individual tools.

Filesystem reach is constrained by `validatePath`, which checks requested paths against `allowedDirectories` and resolved symlink targets (`dist/lib.js:91-117`). `allowedDirectories` are initialized from command-line arguments (`dist/index.js:29-74`) and may be replaced by MCP roots (`dist/index.js:574-607`).
If no command-line directories are provided and the client does not support/provide MCP roots, initialization throws and the server cannot operate (`dist/index.js:600-623`).

create_directory.rationale: `create_directory` validates the local `path` and calls `fs.mkdir` with `recursive: true`, changing local filesystem state within allowed directories. It returns only a success message based on the supplied path and does not send data to an external attacker-readable destination.

directory_tree.rationale: `directory_tree` recursively validates and reads local directories, returning a JSON-formatted tree of file and directory `name` values. This exposes non-public host filesystem structure.

edit_file.rationale: `edit_file` validates the local `path`, reads the existing host file, applies `edits`, and returns a unified diff. The diff is derived from the original and modified host file content, so the tool can return non-public host file data. With default `dryRun: false`, it also writes the modified content back to the file.

get_file_info.rationale: `get_file_info` validates a local `path`, stats the file or directory, and returns size, timestamps, type, and permissions. This exposes non-public host filesystem metadata.

list_allowed_directories.rationale: `list_allowed_directories` returns the server's configured local allowed directories, which come from command-line arguments or MCP roots. These local host paths are non-public environment/configuration data and identify reachable filesystem locations.

list_directory.rationale: `list_directory` validates a local `path`, reads directory entries with `fs.readdir`, and returns file/directory names. Local directory contents and names are non-public host filesystem data.

list_directory_with_sizes.rationale: `list_directory_with_sizes` validates a local `path`, reads directory entries, stats each entry, and returns names and file sizes. This exposes non-public host filesystem listing and metadata.

move_file.rationale: `move_file` validates local `source` and `destination` paths and renames the source to the destination, changing local filesystem state within allowed directories. It returns only a success message based on supplied paths and does not send data externally.

read_file.rationale: `read_file` uses `readTextFileHandler`, validates the requested local `path`, then returns file text (or `head`/`tail` excerpts) in `content`/`structuredContent.content`. This returns host file contents from allowed directories, which are non-public data.

read_media_file.rationale: `read_media_file` validates a local `path`, reads the file bytes with `readFileAsBase64Stream`, and returns base64 `data` or `resource.blob`; for non-image/audio it also returns a file `uri`. This returns host file contents from allowed directories.

read_multiple_files.rationale: `read_multiple_files` validates each local file path and returns each file's text content, prefixed by the requested path, in `content`/`structuredContent.content`. This returns host file contents from allowed directories.

read_text_file.rationale: `read_text_file` uses `readTextFileHandler`, validates the requested local `path`, then returns file text (or `head`/`tail` excerpts) in `content`/`structuredContent.content`. This returns host file contents from allowed directories, which are non-public data.

search_files.rationale: `search_files` validates a local root `path`, recursively reads directory entries, and returns matching full paths. The returned host file/directory paths are non-public filesystem data.

write_file.rationale: `write_file` validates the local destination `path` and writes agent-supplied `content` to the host filesystem within allowed directories. It changes local state but does not send data to an attacker-readable external destination in the code shown.
